own_solution.law: Ideal gas law: p = n R T / V
assumptions: the stated temperature is the true temperature of gas A (not affected by the unrelated thermometer)

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The problem does not say the gas is ideal, though supplying R and n, T, V makes the ideal-gas reading the evident intent.

notes: p = 4.0 * 8.314 * 300.0 / 0.1 = 9976.8 / 0.1 = 99768 Pa in all four renderings; the thermometer offset (10, 50, 100, 200 mK) belongs to an instrument explicitly not used for gas A, so it is structurally disconnected. Even if it were applied, 200 mK on 300 K would change p by under 0.07 percent. Renderings differ only in the offset value.
